_about: The four tasks of studies 4 and 5, shared by efficiency_run.py (study 4) and local_run.py (study 5); study_tasks.py reads this file, builds the prompts, seeds the starting state and runs the success checks. Every check compares against values Kibana or Elasticsearch hold; an answer line counts only when it matches Kibana's actual value. A task's prompt is the arm's preamble, the task's intro and numbered steps, and the task's closing. STUDY_DESIGN.md decision 12 onward.

arms.api: A local Kibana 9.5 is available. Its URL is in the environment variable KIBANA_URL and an API key in KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY. Kibana's API reference is in ./kibana-api/ (kibana.yaml for the whole API, dashboards-api.yaml for the Dashboards and Visualizations APIs).

tasks.label: The web-logs task
tasks.intro: Work on Kibana's web-logs sample data (data view '{data_view}', index {index}). Do these steps in order:

steps.text: Describe the data view '{data_view}': look up its fields and name its time field.
Build a dashboard titled '{marker} Web logs' on that data view with exactly two panels: the number of requests over time, and the number of requests by HTTP response code.

Create an alert rule named '{marker} 5xx errors' on the web-logs data for the signal of the response-code panel: it checks every minute and fires when more than 10 requests with a 5xx response code arrive within 5 minutes. The rule must be enabled when you finish: if it is created disabled, enable it.
Edit the response-code panel of that dashboard: change its title to 'Responses by code'. Then read the alert rule back and check whether it is enabled.

tasks.closing:
When every step is done, end your reply with these two lines:
TIME_FIELD: <the data view's time field>
RULE_ENABLED: <yes or no, as you read it back>

tasks.label: The web-logs task on flights data
tasks.intro: Work on Kibana's flights sample data (data view '{data_view}', index {index}). Do these steps in order:

steps.text: Describe the data view '{data_view}': look up its fields and name its time field.
Build a dashboard titled '{marker} Flights' on that data view with exactly two panels: the number of flights over time, and the number of flights by carrier.

Create an alert rule named '{marker} Cancelled flights' on the flights data: it checks every minute and fires when more than 10 cancelled flights arrive within 5 minutes. The rule must be enabled when you finish: if it is created disabled, enable it.
Edit the carrier panel of that dashboard: change its title to 'Flights by carrier'. Then read the alert rule back and check whether it is enabled.

tasks.closing:
When every step is done, end your reply with these two lines:
TIME_FIELD: <the data view's time field>
RULE_ENABLED: <yes or no, as you read it back>

tasks.label: Change existing objects
tasks.intro: Kibana holds a dashboard titled 'Site health' and an alert rule named 'Server errors', both on the web-logs sample data (data view '{data_view}', index {index}). Change them in place; do not create new dashboards or rules. Do these steps in order:

steps.text: Add a third panel to the 'Site health' dashboard showing the number of requests by host.

tasks.closing: When every step is done, reply with a short summary.

tasks.label: Look up existing objects
tasks.intro: Kibana holds a dashboard titled 'Site health' and an alert rule that watches the web-logs sample data (data view '{data_view}', index {index}) for 5xx responses. Look them up; change nothing. Answer these questions:

steps.text: How many panels does the 'Site health' dashboard have?
What is the name of the alert rule that watches for 5xx responses?
How often does that rule check?

tasks.closing:
End your reply with these four lines:
PANELS: <number>
RULE_NAME: <the rule's name>
INTERVAL: <the check interval, such as 5m>
ENABLED: <yes or no>
